name: weather-app
description: Build a complete weather app that works identically across all variants

promptLevels.beginner: make a Weather class that can fetch and store weather data for cities
promptLevels.intermediate: create a Weather class that fetches weather data from an API, stores current city and weather info, and manages favorites
promptLevels.advanced: write a Weather class that manages weather app state including current city, weather data (temp, conditions, humidity), loading/error states, and a list of favorite cities with persistence
promptLevels.expert: Write a Weather class for managing a weather application's state and data. The class should: 1) Have properties for: currentCity (string), weatherData (object with temperature, description, humidity, windSpeed, etc.), isLoading (boolean), error (string or null), and favoriteCities (array of city names). 2) Have a fetchWeather(cityName) async method that sets isLoading=true, fetches weather data (simulated or real API), updates weatherData and currentCity on success, sets error message on failure, and sets isLoading=false when done. 3) Have addFavorite(cityName) method that adds a city to favorites if not already present. 4) Have removeFavorite(cityName) method that removes a city from favorites. 5) Have getFavorites() method that returns the favorites array. The class should properly manage async state transitions and handle errors gracefully. {languageSpecific}

languageInstructions.typescript: Use TypeScript with interfaces for WeatherData (temperature number, description string, humidity number, windSpeed number, etc.), properties properly typed (currentCity: string | null, weatherData: WeatherData | null, isLoading: boolean, error: string | null, favoriteCities: string[]). The fetchWeather method should return Promise<void>. Export both interfaces and the Weather class.
languageInstructions.javascript: Create a Weather class with constructor initializing all properties to appropriate defaults. Use async/await for fetchWeather. Use array methods for favorites management (includes, push, filter). Export the class as default.
languageInstructions.javascript-jsdoc: Use JSDoc with @typedef for WeatherData object, @class for Weather, @property for all class properties with types, @async for fetchWeather, @param with types, @returns Promise<void> for async methods and appropriate types for others. Export the class.

variants.typescript: Build a Weather class that fetches weather data and manages app state. Include interfaces for weather data, city, and app state.
variants.javascript: Build a Weather class that fetches weather data and manages app state.
variants.javascript-jsdoc: Build a Weather class with complete JSDoc that fetches weather data and manages app state.
variants.javascript-vanilla-web:
Create a complete weather application using vanilla JavaScript. Include:

**Features:**
- Search for city weather
- Display current weather (temp, description, icon, humidity, wind)
- 5-day forecast
- Save favorite cities (localStorage)
- Toggle Celsius/Fahrenheit
- Recent searches (last 5)
- Loading states
- Error handling

**API:**
- Use OpenWeatherMap API or weatherapi.com
- Handle API errors gracefully
- Show user-friendly error messages

**HTML:**
- Search input with autocomplete suggestions
- Current weather display
- Forecast cards
- Favorites sidebar
- Settings (temp unit toggle)

**CSS:**
- Modern, clean design
- Weather icons
- Background changes based on weather
- Mobile responsive
- Smooth transitions

**JavaScript:**
- API service module
- State management
- LocalStorage for persistence
- Event handlers
- Render functions

**Note:** Include mock data or instructions for getting free API key.

Return as single HTML file (or multiple files with clear structure).
variants.javascript-vanilla-web-jsdoc:
Same as javascript-vanilla-web with complete JSDoc annotations:
- @typedef WeatherData
- @typedef City
- @typedef ForecastDay
- @typedef AppState
- Document all functions
- Include module-level documentation
variants.typescript-vanilla-web:
Create a weather app using TypeScript and vanilla Web APIs. Include:

**TypeScript:**
- Interface for WeatherData, City, Forecast, AppState
- Type-safe API service
- Generic storage utility with types
- Proper event typing

**Architecture:**
- Module structure:
  - api.ts (API calls)
  - types.ts (interfaces)
  - state.ts (state management)
  - storage.ts (localStorage wrapper)
  - render.ts (UI rendering)
  - main.ts (app initialization)

**Features:**
- All features from javascript-vanilla-web
- Full type safety
- No frameworks

Provide TypeScript source files and HTML structure.
variants.typescript-react:
Create a weather app using TypeScript React. Include:

**Components:**
- App (main)
- SearchBar (with autocomplete)
- CurrentWeather (current conditions)
- Forecast (5-day forecast)
- ForecastCard (individual day)
- Favorites (saved cities)
- Settings (temp unit toggle)

**Custom Hooks:**
- useWeather (fetch and manage weather data)
- useLocalStorage<T> (generic localStorage hook)
- useDebounce (for search autocomplete)

**Context:**
- WeatherContext (global settings, favorites)
- TypeScript for all context types

**TypeScript:**
- Interfaces for all data types
- Type-safe hooks
- Proper component prop types
- Generic utilities

**Features:**
- All features from vanilla versions
- React best practices
- Performance optimizations (memo, useMemo, useCallback)
- Error boundaries

**State Management:**
- Context API only (no Redux, Zustand, etc.)
- Type-safe throughout

Minimal dependencies (React, ReactDOM only).
